purpose: Selexipag is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps slow down the worsening of this condition and reduces the chances of being hospitalized. It can help you breathe more easily and do more of your daily activities.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a substance called prostacyclin that helps keep blood vessels relaxed and open. In PAH, this system does not work well enough, causing the blood vessels in your lungs to tighten and narrow. Selexipag mimics prostacyclin by attaching to the same receptors, helping to widen those blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood through your lungs.
common_side_effects: Headache, jaw pain, pain in your arms or legs, flushing (feeling of warmth or redness), nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting are common, especially when you first start or increase your dose. These effects often get better over time as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not take selexipag if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control while on this medication. Tell your doctor right away if you notice signs of low blood pressure such as dizziness or fainting. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as stopping abruptly can make your condition worse.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 200 micrograms (mcg) twice a day, taken with food. Every week, your doctor may increase your dose by 200 mcg twice a day until you reach the highest dose that works well for you without causing too many side effects. The maximum dose is 1,600 mcg twice daily. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
